what: the corpus lane's spelling bridge: the 1,173 places where our text spells a word otherwise than the Leningrad text STEP and MACULA follow, each with its class and, at 1,035 of them, STEP's pieces cut onto our letters. Kept here byte for byte in the folders the lane keeps them in: v1 (relay v202) with its rule, its receipt and, beside it, the lane's list of the 9 form rows not landed; and v1.1 (relay v214), v1's lines with each piece's part of STEP's column as STEP writes it, with its rule and its receipt; and v1.2 (relay v220), v1.1's lines with STEP's «{…}+» tags read as STEP's key says, with its rule, its receipt and its list of changes, the list laid since ship 20 (23 November 2026). tools/apply-spelling-bridge-v1.mjs lays the place's pieces on the zone at the kinds named under `laid`, and the reader draws the place's line from them as it does at every place that carries pieces. What a zone carries for a place is said once, in tools/spelling-bridge-v1.mjs

form_rows.kept_by: data/landings/PIN.json, which lands these rows (ship 11c); read here only as the same bytes

v1_1.what: v1's lines in v1's order, every v1 field as v1 wrote it, with three fields more: on each piece its part of STEP's Translation column as STEP writes it (english_tahot_as_written, brackets and the space after the stroke kept) and where it comes from (english_tahot_as_written_from), and on each line its rows' columns whole (translation_columns_as_tahot_writes_them). Read only where each line, its added fields taken off, is v1's line
v1_1.why_not_kept: as for v1: the lane's folder also holds its answer, its builder, its second count with that count's receipt and two runs, and its checker's recount; no tool reads them, and each is named here by the bytes and sha256 the relay's letter gives

v1_2.what: v1.1's lines in v1.1's order, read as STEP's key reads its tag column: «{H…}+» is the word's own tag, in braces, and the same tag also covers the next Hebrew word. v1 took one brace off each end, so 43 pieces at 43 places carried a tag like «H4648G}+» and were not read as the word's own. v1.2 gives each the number STEP names, reads the roles again at 7 places (13 pieces) and the main tags at the 43 (with their glosses, and the store's counts at 2): 147 fields, each named in changes-v1.2.jsonl with v1.1's value and v1.2's. On every piece three fields more, right after its tag: the tag as TAHOT writes it, whether it covers the next Hebrew word, and that word. Read only where each line, its three added fields taken off and its changes set back, is v1.1's line. Ship 20 (23 November 2026) lays from it in place of v1.1: no laid place moves, and the 42 places of new pieces held for the «}+» tag fall to the holds of call 4 they stand under
v1_2.why_not_kept: as for v1 and v1.1: the lane's folder also holds its answer, its builder, its second count with that count's receipt and two runs, and its checker's recount; no tool reads them, and each is named here by the bytes and sha256 the relay's letter gives. The same relay's count of the same fault in lattice v12 and the zones served (lattice-plus-tags-v1/) finds no served reading wrong and lands nothing

held_with_call_4.why: the places call 4 holds as they rest are read where the hold itself is read: call 4's landing in the audit calls' pin, while it still holds the class of STEP's words written with « | », and the list it names, the same bytes the default picks' bake reads through its own pin (held_split_v189); every place whose STEP's words hold « | », the bake's own rule; and, while that landing lands the action stands_action, every place of the list with that action whose STEP's words hold no « | », where STEP's own reading stands. Never a list of places of its own (22 November 2026)

laid.why: STEP's spelling column writes our letters at the place and cuts them, and one form row of the same relay is STEP's own row for the place. The place's pieces are our letters as the list cuts them, and each piece's English is that row's own words cut at the stroke, as STEP writes them, brackets and all. The list's English for the same piece is held equal to it, the brackets aside

our letters and the Leningrad text's differ by one letter, and the corpus lane's bridge cuts STEP's pieces onto ours through it. Bridge v1.1 (relay v214) gives each piece its part of STEP's Translation column as STEP writes it, brackets and all; the piece's English is that part with the spaces taken off its ends, as the lane's letter says to do when the pieces are joined, and the marks taken off the part give v1's English for the piece, held so at every piece. The places where call 4 of relay v189 makes STEP's own reading stand are held (not_laid)

not_laid.why: call 4 of relay v189 writes STEP's words here with « | », one written word read as two of STEP's, and the house holds the place's line as it rests until the corpus lane says how STEP's line reads there (the owner's question 2, put back to the lane; the audit calls' pin, call 4's holds). The bridge does not lay pieces past that hold (the page lane's call, 22 November 2026): at Psalms 44:15 they would print «not + peoples» where the word reads «among the peoples». Read as the hold is read (held_with_call_4), so that when the lane answers call 4 the same rule lets them in. 40 of the 46 were held for STEP's «}+» tag until bridge v1.2 (relay v220, ship 20, 23 November 2026) gave each piece the number STEP names; each is a place call 4 holds too

the place is a pair in our text: the lattice's surface writes a written form and a read form (round and square brackets), the zone's word there is a pair, whose line a zone carries by its own rule, and the bridge lays pieces on a plain word only

call 4 of relay v189 makes STEP's own pick 1 the line here whatever today's line is, and the page asks it before the place's pieces. Laid in ship 17's first build, the pieces left the line as it was and read the place a second way beside it: the card opened on the whole word, STEP's pick pressed, with the place's pieces said above it (check-compspan-coverage-v1 C3, Amos 1:10), and under a source pressed a reading across two words kept the pieces where the line as it rests is STEP's words (check-rulings-under-sources-v1 U8, Esther 9:18). The owner ruled on 23 November 2026 («steps is fine»): STEP's reading governs the card at these places, and the pieces are not laid. Read from call 4's list as the hold above is, while its landing lands the action named (held_with_call_4.stands_action). 2 of the 726 (Numbers 33:35 word 4, Numbers 33:36 word 2) were held for STEP's «}+» tag until bridge v1.2 (relay v220, ship 20, 23 November 2026)

tags: not written in this pass. The list gives each piece its tag, and the place's entry would be its core piece's. A zone's tag is the lattice's (check-entry-gate-v1 holds each tagged word to the lattice's core tags), so the place keeps what it carries: the entries of MACULA's lemma at 192 of the 206, none at 14. At 205 of the 206 the core piece's number is among the entries the place is asked already, or the place is asked none Ship 17 (22 November 2026) writes none at the places it lays, for the same reason: a zone's tag is the lattice's, and teaching the projector and the entry gate the bridge is a ship of its own
lifted_by: the lane's next lattice, where it reads these places under our spelling and gives them pieces itself. The tool refuses a place that carries other pieces than these, and this pin is retired then
note: every sha256 here is the one the relay's letter names for the file (v202's for bridge-v1, v214's for bridge-v1.1, v220's for bridge-v1.2), and the lane's receipts name the lists by the same; v1.1's receipt also names v1's files it was built from, and v1.2's v1.1's, by the same. Which kinds are laid is the page lane's decision, set here as data so neither the tool nor the check carries a list of its own; the counts beside each kind are the list's, recounted by both. A kind is a class, its use and, for a place of new pieces, what holds it within its class (`held`, said in tools/spelling-bridge-v1.mjs). The 206 places ship 11d laid on 21 November are worded by their form rows (`words`: form_row), each form row's part held to v1.1's part byte for byte; the places ship 17 lays on 22 November by v1.1's parts (`words`: as_written)
